headline: 14,000 new recruits: Police to hire 6,000 constables and 4,000 SIs
summary: The government has approved the direct recruitment of 4,000 Sub-Inspectors and plans to hire 6,000 constables through the current recruitment process.
details: Bangladesh Police is set to recruit 6,000 constables under the current recruitment cycle. This includes filling 2,000 existing vacancies and adding 4,000 new positions from a proposed 10,000-post expansion.

headline: Messi magic seals Miami’s comeback win with goal and assist
summary: Lionel Messi scored his MLS-leading 26th goal and provided an assist to lift Inter Miami to a 2-1 victory, moving them to second place in the Eastern Conference.
details: Lionel Messi scored his MLS-leading 26th goal in the 83rd minute to lift visiting Inter Miami to a 2-1 victory over the New England Revolution on Sunday night. The win has major playoff seeding implications for both teams.
Messi also assisted German Berterame's 69th-minute equalizer for Inter Miami. The team moved above New England into second place in the Eastern Conference with one regular-season match remaining.

Telasco Segovia provided assists on both goals as Inter Miami snapped a two-match winless run. Daniel Gazdag had scored in the 53rd minute for New England, which failed to extend its four-match winning streak.

Messi was the primary architect of his own matchwinner, picking up a loose ball about 30 yards from goal before slaloming through multiple New England defenders. Segovia kept the play alive, allowing Messi to score.
The Revolution had an apparent own-goal equalizer overturned in the 87th minute after a video review ruled a player offside on the play.
New England started the second half better, with Peyton Miller setting up Daniel Gazdag's go-ahead goal. Ilay Feingold added a backheeled touch to set up Gazdag's shot past the goalkeeper.
That goal sparked Miami into action. Messi forced a diving save in the 65th minute before a teammate cleared a rebound off the line. Segovia then lofted a pass for Messi's equalizer assist.
The victory moved Inter Miami (16-6-11, 59 points) above New England (18-11-4, 58 points) in the Eastern Conference standings.
caption:
Lionel Messi delivered a goal and an assist to secure a crucial 2-1 comeback victory for Inter Miami against the New England Revolution.

Lionel Messi scored his MLS-leading 26th goal in the 83rd minute to lift visiting Inter Miami to a 2-1 victory over the New England Revolution on Sunday night. The win has major playoff seeding implications for both teams.

Messi also assisted German Berterame's 69th-minute equalizer for Inter Miami. The team moved above New England into second place in the Eastern Conference with one regular-season match remaining.

Telasco Segovia provided assists on both goals as Inter Miami snapped a two-match winless run. Daniel Gazdag had scored in the 53rd minute for New England, which failed to extend its four-match winning streak.

Messi was the primary architect of his own matchwinner, picking up a loose ball about 30 yards from goal before slaloming through multiple New England defenders. Segovia kept the play alive, allowing Messi to score.

The Revolution had an apparent own-goal equalizer overturned in the 87th minute after a video review ruled a player offside on the play.

New England started the second half better, with Peyton Miller setting up Daniel Gazdag's go-ahead goal. Ilay Feingold added a backheeled touch to set up Gazdag's shot past the goalkeeper.

That goal sparked Miami into action. Messi forced a diving save in the 65th minute before a teammate cleared a rebound off the line. Segovia then lofted a pass for Messi's equalizer assist.

The victory moved Inter Miami (16-6-11, 59 points) above New England (18-11-4, 58 points) in the Eastern Conference standings.
